root_cause.text: The ksmbd TCP connection setup path in fs/smb/server/transport_tcp.c failed to roll back the previously incremented active_num_conn when alloc_transport() returned NULL in ksmbd_tcp_new_connection(), causing the max-connections counter to leak on allocation failure.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “ksmbd_kthread_fn() increments active_num_conn before calling ksmbd_tcp_new_connection() … so when alloc_transport() returns NULL the socket is released and -ENOMEM returned without decrementing the counter,” and the patch adds `if (server_conf.max_connections) atomic_dec(&active_num_conn);` exactly in the `if (!t)` alloc_transport failure path.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states “ksmbd_kthread_fn() increments active_num_conn before calling ksmbd_tcp_new_connection() … so when alloc_transport() returns NULL the socket is released and -ENOMEM returned without decrementing the counter,” and the patch adds `if (server_conf.max_connections) atomic_dec(&active_num_conn);` exactly in the `if (!t)` alloc_transport failure path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Decrement the active connection count on transport allocation failure so max_connections tracking stays accurate.
intent_record.what: In the allocation failure path of ksmbd_tcp_new_connection(), after sock_release(client_sk) and before returning -ENOMEM, the code now conditionally calls atomic_dec(&active_num_conn) when server_conf.max_connections is nonzero.
intent_record.how: This restores the active connection counter when alloc_transport(client_sk) fails after a connection had already been counted, preventing the runtime connection count from remaining artificially elevated and incorrectly consuming available connection slots when max_connections enforcement is enabled.

grouping_result.intent: Decrement the active connection count on transport allocation failure so max_connections tracking stays accurate.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the stated root cause by rolling back the incremented active connection count when alloc_transport() fails, preventing max_connections counter leakage.

candidates.rationale: On alloc_transport() failure, this error return exits without rolling back the previously incremented active_num_conn, directly causing the leaked active connection count.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early error return in ksmbd_tcp_new_connection() executes after the active connection count was incremented but before it is rolled back when alloc_transport() fails, causing active_num_conn to leak and max-connections accounting to become inaccurate.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient to inspect the alloc_transport() failure path. The root cause described requires a previously incremented active_num_conn to be rolled back when alloc_transport(client_sk) returns NULL. In this snippet, the relevant path is only `t = alloc_transport(client_sk); if (!t) return -ENOMEM;` (lines 189-191). There is no increment of `active_num_conn` in this function body, and no rollback/decrement logic either. Because the vulnerable construct as described is the missing rollback of a previously incremented counter in `ksmbd_tcp_new_connection()`, and that counter manipulation is completely absent from the provided code, this function body does not itself contain the vulnerable construct. It also does not contain the fix, since there is no compensating decrement or rollback before the `return -ENOMEM;`.
